<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/">Resolving a request</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Five steps from bytes to entry point, forwarded headers that are read only from a trusted peer, and a trailing slash that means something.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#a-request-resolves-in-five-steps">A request resolves by longest mount match, prefix strip, static file, path dispatch, then the entry — and production runs only match, strip, entry</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#trusted-proxies-is-empty-and-empty-reads-nothing"><code>trusted_proxies</code> defaults to empty, empty means the forwarded headers are never read, and a trusted walk takes the rightmost untrusted <code>X-Forwarded-For</code> entry</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#x-forwarded-for-is-the-only-address-header"><code>X-Forwarded-For</code> is the only client-address header read; a trusted peer sending another is warned about, and an untrusted header is ignored, never refused</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#a-forwarded-token-is-read-withheld-or-refused">A forwarded token's port is removed, a withheld address answers <code>null</code>, and a token that neither names nor withholds one is a <code>400</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#x-forwarded-proto-sets-the-scheme-and-hsts-only">A trusted <code>X-Forwarded-Proto</code> sets the effective scheme and HSTS emission and feeds nothing else; no <code>X-Forwarded-Host</code> is read</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#host-matching-is-on-the-host-part-only">An absent <code>Host</code> is a <code>400</code>; matching strips the port, folds ASCII case and one trailing dot, refuses non-ASCII, and an unknown host on a host-mounted deployment is a <code>404</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#a-path-is-never-derived-from-a-url">A filesystem path is never derived from a URL at request time</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/resolving-a-request/#a-trailing-slash-is-never-normalised">A trailing slash is never normalised: <code>/users</code> and <code>/users/</code> are two URIs</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/">Methods, bodies and static files</a><span class="nv-section-count">7</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">HEAD runs as GET, a preflight is answered before any code runs, and a route that never reads a body allocates nothing.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#head-runs-as-get"><code>HEAD</code> runs as <code>GET</code> with the body discarded and <code>Content-Length</code> kept; <code>method()</code> reports <code>Get</code> and <code>isHead()</code> tells the truth</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#a-preflight-is-answered-before-any-code-runs">A CORS preflight is answered from <code>[http.cors]</code> before the unit is loaded, and a plain <code>OPTIONS</code> is passed through</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#the-body-is-read-on-demand-under-two-caps"><code>[limits] request_body</code> bounds bytes parsed into memory and <code>upload_total</code> bounds a streamed multipart body, each with a hard ceiling, and a route that never reads a body allocates nothing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#buffering-readers-share-the-body-and-streaming-readers-consume-it">A buffering body reader keeps what it read so another may follow it, and a streaming one consumes the body and is the only reader of it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#static-serving-is-one-policy">Static serving is one policy in both modes: the exact file, never a listing, one <code>ETag</code>, one <code>Range</code>, and a <code>.nvs</code> file is never served as source</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#health-path-is-off-and-checks-nothing"><code>health_path</code> is off by default; set, it answers <code>200</code> while accepting and <code>503</code> while draining, and checks no dependency</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/methods-bodies-and-static-files/#the-trace-id-is-the-request-identifier">The trace id exists on every request regardless of sampling, is the only request identifier, is emitted on the response, and an inbound <code>X-Request-ID</code> is ignored</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/">Response headers, CORS and cookies</a><span class="nv-section-count">7</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">What a deployment that configured nothing already sends, and why CORS stays closed until an origin is named.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#the-access-log-is-a-mode-default"><code>[log] access</code> is a mode default — on in development, off in PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#secure-headers-with-nothing-written">A deployment that wrote no <code>[http.headers]</code> already sends class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#hsts-follows-the-effective-scheme">HSTS is emitted when the effective href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#cors-is-closed-until-origins-are-named">CORS is closed until <code>[http.cors] origins</code> names one: no header is emitted and a preflight is href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#a-wildcard-origin-with-credentials-is-refused"><code>origins = [&quot;*&quot;]</code> with <code>credentials = true</code> is refused at boot and at runtime alike, and so is <code>same_site = &quot;None&quot;</code> without <code>secure</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#cookies-are-secure-httponly-and-lax">Every cookie <code>Core\Response::addCookie</code> writes is <code>Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/</code> unless the call site says otherwise</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/headers-cors-and-cookies/#policy-headers-are-runtime-class-and-setheader-wins">Every <code>[http.headers]</code>, <code>[http.cors]</code> and <code>[http.cookies]</code> directive is <code>Runtime</code> class, and <code>Core\Response::setHeader</code> overrides a policy-owned header on one response without logging</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>

<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/">Sessions</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A session is a record its store issued. Four operations, loaded once, written whole only when it changed, and never locked.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#a-session-store-answers-four-operations">A session is a record its store issued: a backend answers <code>issue</code>, <code>load</code>, <code>save</code> and <code>destroy</code>, and <code>load</code> answering absent is the whole of the strict-id rule</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#session-backend-is-shared-or-db-and-local-is-refused-at-boot"><code>[session] backend</code> admits <code>shared</code> and <code>db</code>, and writing <code>local</code> is a boot refusal naming the file it was written in</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#no-session-block-means-no-store">A tree with no <code>[session]</code> block has no session store, and <code>start</code> throws naming the block to write</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#a-session-is-loaded-once-and-written-whole">A session record is loaded once at <code>start</code>, written back whole only when it changed, and never locked</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#session-expiry-belongs-to-the-store"><code>[session] ttl</code> is written onto the record and the store expires it; there is no sweeper and no probability of one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/sessions/#a-session-holds-a-secret-only-sealed">A user's own secret lives in their session, sealed under a key ring through <code>setSecret</code> and <code>getSecret</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/">Uploads</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Parts arrive lazily through one member, bounded by two separate caps, and there is no temporary file anywhere.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#an-upload-is-received-only-through-files"><code>Core\Request::files()</code> yields uploaded parts lazily, one at a time, and is the only way to receive one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#a-part-is-a-file-iff-it-carries-a-filename">A part is a file part iff its <code>Content-Disposition</code> carries <code>filename</code>; every other part is buffered into <code>post()</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#a-part-is-consumed-in-one-of-three-ways">A part is consumed by <code>readAll</code>, by walking <code>content()</code>, or by <code>saveTo</code>, and each way is bounded</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#request-body-and-upload-total-are-two-caps"><code>request_body</code> caps bytes parsed into memory and <code>upload_total</code> caps a streamed multipart body, and both are <code>[limits]</code> rows</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#upload-total-is-enforced-on-the-wire"><code>upload_total</code> is enforced by the server on the wire: a declared oversize is refused before dispatch and a chunked one is stopped at the part being read</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/uploads/#there-is-no-temp-file">There is no temp file: a part lands on disk only where the application names a path under <code>fs.write</code>, and disk is the resource it must bound</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>

<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/">The HTTP client</a><span class="nv-section-count">20</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">No spelling for &quot;wait forever&quot;, one deadline over the whole call, opt-in jittered retry, and an address pinned before connecting.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#no-spelling-for-an-unbounded-wait"><code>Core\Http\Client</code> has no spelling for &quot;wait forever&quot;: every bound is a <code>Duration</code>, an omitted one inherits <code>[http.client]</code>, and expiry throws <code>TimeoutError</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" approved address, and the connection is made to one of them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-call-tries-every-approved-address">Every address a name resolves to is checked, one denied refuses the host, and the call falls back across the approved set without ever resolving twice</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-call-names-its-address-only-under-a-grant"><code>connectTo</code> names an outbound call's address only where <code>net.connect_to</code> names the host, and the address policy and the certificate's host check still apply</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#redirects-are-off-and-every-hop-is-re-pinned">Redirects are not followed by default; when enabled every hop is re-checked and re-pinned, a denied hop fails the request, and a retry never re-resolves</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-https-redirect-never-becomes-plaintext">A redirect from <code>https</code> to <code>http</code> needs <code>net.downgrade</code> for its host and <code>redirectToHttp</code> at the call; a plain <code>http</code> URL asked for directly stays allowed</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#a-cross-origin-redirect-drops-credentials">A redirect hop to another origin carries none of the caller's own headers, the three named credentials and every <code>secret</code> value among them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-connection-is-pooled-per-core-and-stays-pinned">An outbound connection is pooled per core under a key carrying everything the check approved, and returns to the pool only after a reply read to the end under known framing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-proxy-is-operator-configured"><code>[http.client.proxy]</code> is the only way an outbound call is proxied: <code>System</code> class, written by the operator, and never a call option or an environment variable</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#a-proxied-call-keeps-its-pin-unless-the-operator-says-otherwise"><code>resolve</code> is mandatory: <code>local</code> tunnels to the address Novis approved and keeps the pin, <code>proxy</code> narrows the policy to the URL's text and warns at every boot</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#the-client-trust-roots-are-the-operators"><code>[http.client.tls]</code> is the operator's alone: the bundled roots unless files are named, TLS 1.2 unless the floor is raised, and no key log in <code>production</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#a-reply-reports-its-tls-session"><code>Response::tls()</code> reports the session a reply arrived over — version, cipher, whether the peer was verified, and its chain — and is <code>null</code> when there was none</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-socket-is-opened-like-an-outbound-call">A WebSocket is opened by <code>Core\Http\Client::openSocket</code> under every rule an outbound call obeys, <code>ws</code> and <code>wss</code> serve that row alone, and a socket is never pooled</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-socket-belongs-to-the-task-that-opened-it">An outbound socket is charged to the task that opened it and closed with <code>1001</code> when that task ends, and it is never a root isolate</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/the-http-client/#an-outbound-socket-is-bounded-by-idle-a-lifetime-and-a-message-cap"><code>idle</code>, <code>maxDuration</code>, <code>maxMessage</code> and <code>sendTimeout</code> bound every outbound socket, each inherits a finite default, and none has an unbounded spelling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/">Containment</a><span class="nv-section-count">13</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Nothing a request can send terminates a worker. Four bounded tiers, a watchdog that sheds rather than kills, and one stated residue.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#a-requests-blast-radius-is-bounded-at-four-tiers">Nothing a request can send terminates or wedges a worker: its blast radius is bounded at four named tiers, and the residue is one stated fault class</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#containment-does-not-end-at-the-helper">A worker task's root is wrapped in <code>catch_unwind</code>: a panic beneath a request fails that request, and one outside any request retires the worker</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#engine-depth-is-bounded-per-decoder">Every engine-side recursive descent over request data carries a depth counter and refuses past it, with a limit per decoder and <code>512</code> for JSON</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper">A helper whose runtime scales with its input polls the request's deadline flag through a bounded-loop combinator, or bounds its input instead</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#no-path-reaches-abort">No path reaches <code>abort()</code>: nothing on a teardown path panics, teardown is iterative, and an allocation sized by request data is fallible</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#a-core-is-never-blocked-on-a-syscall">A core is never blocked on a syscall: filesystem calls, name resolution and waiting on a child go to a blocking pool bounded at twice the core count</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#a-wedged-core-is-detected-by-its-deadline">A watchdog reads the in-flight deadline each worker already keeps, and reports a core whose oldest deadline is past by a margin</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#a-wedged-core-is-shed-never-killed">A reported core stops accepting and <code>max_in_flight</code> counts its share as unavailable; a wedged worker is never killed in-process</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#an-abandoned-request-is-cancelled-at-the-drop">A client that goes away cancels its request tree at the next safepoint; nothing is waited out</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#every-deadline-is-monotonic">Every timeout, deadline and backoff in the engine is computed on a monotonic clock</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#the-floor-cannot-fill-the-disk">The floor cannot fill the disk it writes to: a file target rotates under a retention bound, repeats coalesce into one record with a count, and a cache write failure compiles in memory</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#a-jit-page-is-never-writable-and-executable-at-once">A page holding generated code is writable while written and executable only after being made read-only</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/http-server/containment/#the-residue-is-one-named-fault-class">A memory-safety fault in <code>unsafe</code> code or a miscompile is the one residue: the process dies, the supervisor restarts it, and the answer is frequency, not a boundary</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
</div>
